chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated from his father, from Al-Nawfaly, from Al-Sakoony, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon them) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:

The worst affliction is when a man is brought forward and his neck is struck off (beheaded); and the captive as long as he is in the chains of the enemy; and the man who finds another man on the belly of his wife.

key_terms.يَجِدُ: Finds (in the context of discovering a state or person)

ai.seo_question: What are the three worst afflictions mentioned in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights these three afflictions as the most severe trials, emphasizing the visceral pain of sudden decapitation, the prolonged humiliation of captivity, and the acute emotional distress of marital infidelity. In Shia tradition, this hadith underscores the fragility of human dignity and the specific vulnerabilities associated with death, war, and family life.
